summary.text: 电 is the standardized simplified form of 電, the character for lightning and, in modern use, electricity. In 電, 雨 marks the weather category; 申 is interpreted as a lightning image and is also proposed as a sound component.

formation.text: Traditional 電 combines 雨, which marks the weather category, with 申, interpreted as depicting lightning and proposed as a sound component. Historical pronunciation comparisons support the sound analysis, but the date and original intention of this combination remain unsettled.

components.text: In 電, 雨 marks the weather category associated with lightning. Its role when the graph was first formed remains uncertain.
In 電, 申 is interpreted as depicting lightning and is also proposed as a sound component. The historical sound comparison is plausible, but does not settle the graph’s original intention.

sound_limitation.text: Modern readings are attested, but they do not establish the historical sound relationship or the original graphic intention.

sound.text: These Zhengzhang Old Chinese reconstructions offer a plausible sound comparison, though their details differ.
In Modern Standard Mandarin, 申 is shēn and 電 is diàn; this present-day pair does not establish their historical sound relationship.

history.text: Catalogues identify 電 on a late Western Zhou bronze and in a Warring States Chu manuscript. These attestations show the graph was in use by those periods, but do not establish its earliest occurrence or the bronze inscription’s meaning.
申 is interpreted as an early graph for lightning and is also reported as a graph used for the earthly branch. When 雨 was added to form 電 remains unresolved.
电 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 電; the date and specific graphic steps of simplification remain unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The evidence supports analyzing 雨 as semantic and 申 as pictorial and probably phonetic, but does not resolve when they were combined or the original intention of the combination. Reconstructed pronunciations vary by system and do not by themselves prove graphic intention.
The simplified counterpart is identified, but the date and graphic steps of simplification are unresolved.

senses.period: received Book of Songs; composition date unresolved
senses.text: 電 is used for lightning in a received Book of Songs passage. Its composition date is not independently established, and the late Western Zhou bronze example does not by itself show the word’s meaning there.

senses.period: modern; scientific sense reported from the late nineteenth century
senses.text: 電 is used for electricity and related modern meanings. The precise development from atmospheric lightning to the scientific sense remains unresolved.

developments.text: Both uses are established, but the semantic steps connecting them remain unresolved.

limitations.text: The earliest secure written occurrence and the precise first attestations of electrical and related modern senses remain unresolved.

overview.text: 电 is the simplified form of 電, used for lightning and modern electricity. In 電, 雨 marks the weather category, while 申 is interpreted as a lightning image and may also cue the sound.

components.text: In 電, 雨 points to the weather category associated with lightning.
申 is interpreted as a lightning image. Its proposed sound role fits a plausible Old Chinese comparison, though the reconstructed readings differ in detail.

takeaway.text: The modern electricity sense is established, but its precise development from lightning remains unresolved.

relationships.text: 电 is identified as the simplified form of traditional 電; the date and graphic steps of simplification remain unresolved.
In traditional 電, 雨 marks the weather category; when it was added and its original intention remain unresolved.
申 is interpreted as a lightning image in 電; this interpretation has not been independently confirmed by inspection of early forms.
申 is proposed as a sound component in 電, supported by a plausible but nonidentical reconstructed sound comparison.
